root.name: King's Indian Attack: Yugoslav Variation
root.moves: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. g3 d5 3. Bg2 c6 4. O-O Bg4

overview: Black develops the c8 bishop outside the pawn chain with ...Bg4 before ...e6, then plays ...Nbd7 and ...e5. White keeps the KIA set-up with d3, Nbd2 and e4, and the game is a slow centre fight in which both sides build pawn chains and manoeuvre. Play is sound and theory is modest.

white_ideas.idea: Play d3, Nbd2 and e4 to gain central space, then expand with h3 and kingside pawns.
Use the long diagonal with Bg2 and aim at a kingside attack once e4-e5 is possible.

black_ideas.idea: Establish ...Nbd7, ...e5 and ...Bc5 or ...Be7 for a Philidor-like centre.
Pressure e4 and play ...Qc7 and ...O-O-O or ...O-O with queenside counterplay.

typical_structures.structure: White d3/e4 against Black d5/e5 or e6 with c6; centre kept in tension.

character.notes: Quiet KIA manoeuvring with no forcing lines.

structure.notes: Flank set-up with an undecided centre.

approach.notes: KIA is a set-up White can play against nearly anything; here it meets the ...Bg4 Black set-up.

level.notes: Clear plans, little theory, but must handle the move orders.

character.reason: Quiet pawn chains and few ways to lose quickly.

structure.reason: Flank set-up with an undecided centre.

approach.reason: KIA can be played against almost anything.

level.reason: Modest theory but this Black set-up needs care.

plans.reason: White's Bg2 and eventual e4-e5 push.
